title: Canonical proper-support pullback map
statement:
Let $\Lambda$ be a commutative ring. Let
$$X'\xrightarrow{a}X,\; f'\downarrow,\; f\downarrow,\; Y'\xrightarrow{b}Y$$
be a Cartesian square of schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-pc-fibre-product], with $f$ separated and locally of finite type [def-weil-proper-morphism, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Let $F$ be a sheaf of $\Lambda$-modules on $X_{\mathrm{et}}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves]. Use direct image and constant-coefficient inverse image [def-weil-pbc-direct-image, def-weil-pbc-inverse-image, prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact]. Suppose $G\subseteq f_*F$ and $H\subseteq f'_*a^{-1}F$ are subsheaves with the following section descriptions. For every etale $U\to Y$, $G(U)$ consists of the sections of $F(X\times_YU)$ whose closed support is proper over $U$; for every etale $V\to Y'$, $H(V)$ consists of the sections of $(a^{-1}F)(X'\times_{Y'}V)$ whose closed support is proper over $V$. Here support is the locus of nonzero geometric germs [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks], and a closed subset is proper over its base if its reduced induced closed subscheme is proper [def-weil-pbc-closed-subset-proper-over-base].
There is a canonical $\Lambda$-linear sheaf morphism $\alpha:G\to b_*H$, natural in $F$, whose component on each etale $U\to Y$ sends $s\in G(U)$ to its unit pullback on
$$X'\times_{Y'}(U\times_YY')\cong(X\times_YU)\times_YY'.$$
The support of this image section is exactly the inverse image of $\operatorname{Supp}(s)$ under the displayed projection to $X\times_YU$.

proof.text: For an etale $U\to Y$, put $U'=U\times_Y Y'$, $T_U=X\times_Y U$, and $T'_U=X'\times_{Y'}U'$. The universal property of the fibre product gives $T'_U\cong T_U\times_X X'\cong T_U\times_U U'$; write $q_U:T'_U\to T_U$ for the projection. The constant-coefficient module adjunction for $a$ has a $\Lambda$-linear unit $\eta_{a,F}:F\to a_*a^{-1}F$, with underlying abelian unit the usual one. Evaluate it on the etale object $T_U\to X$. The direct-image formula identifies its target with $(a^{-1}F)(T'_U)$, giving the canonical linear map $t_U(s)=\eta_{a,F}(T_U)(s)$. This construction is defined on all of $F(T_U)$ before imposing support conditions.

source.place: Tag 0F55 (lemma-base-change-f-shriek-separated), ordinary pullback map; etale-cohomology.tex equation-pullback and definition-pullback

proof.text: Fix a geometric point $\bar z':\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to T'_U$. Let $\bar z=q_U\bar z'$ and let $\bar x'$ be its image in $X'$. Apply the inverse-image stalk-and-germ comparison to $a:X'\to X$, the point $\bar x'$, the underlying abelian sheaf of $F$, and the pointed etale neighbourhood $(T_U,\bar z)$ of $a\bar x'$. The induced pointed neighbourhood in $X'$ is $(T_U\times_X X',\bar z')$. Its germ formula gives $c_{a,\bar x',F}((t_U(s))_{\bar z'})=s_{\bar z}$. Since $c$ is a group isomorphism, the left germ is nonzero if and only if the right germ is nonzero. The zero-open criterion says these tests depend only on the underlying points of $T'_U$ and $T_U$. Therefore $\operatorname{Supp}(t_U(s))=q_U^{-1}(\operatorname{Supp}(s))$. The module comparison in Step 1 ensures that this is the germ of the very section constructed there.

source.place: Tag 03Q1 (lemma-stalk-pullback) (3), direct proof and equation-pullback; Tag 04FR (lemma-zero-over-image) (3)

proof.text: If $s\in G(U)$, its closed support $C\subseteq T_U$ is proper over $U$ by hypothesis. The map $T_U\to U$ is locally of finite type, since it is the base change of $f$. Apply clause (1) of the closed-proper-support locality lemma to this map, $C$, and $U'\to U$. It says that $q_U^{-1}(C)$ is a closed subset proper over $U'$. By Step 2 this is exactly the support of $t_U(s)$, so the given section description of $H$ places $t_U(s)$ in $H(U')=(b_*H)(U)$. Thus $t_U$ restricts to a linear map $\alpha_U:G(U)\to(b_*H)(U)$.

For an arrow $r:V\to U$ over $Y$, the induced arrows $T_V\to T_U$ and $T'_V\to T'_U$ are base changes of $r$. Since $\eta_{a,F}$ is a morphism of sheaves, its components satisfy $t_V(s|_{T_V})=t_U(s)|_{T'_V}$. The restriction maps of $G$ and $H$ are the restrictions of their ambient direct images, since they are subsheaves. Both sides belong to $H(V\times_Y Y')$ by Step 3, so the equality in the ambient module is the equality $\alpha_V(s|_V)=\alpha_U(s)|_{V\times_Y Y'}$. Consequently the components $\alpha_U$ define a $\Lambda$-linear sheaf morphism $\alpha:G\to b_*H$. Its component formula fixes it uniquely, which also proves its canonicity.

source.place: Tag 0F55 (lemma-base-change-f-shriek-separated), maps given by pulling back local sections

proof.text: For a module-sheaf morphism $\varphi:F\to\widetilde F$, geometric germs give $\operatorname{Supp}(\varphi(s))\subseteq\operatorname{Supp}(s)$, because $\varphi_{\bar z}(0)=0$. The zero-open criterion makes the first support closed. Clause (2) of the closed-subset properness properties then makes it proper whenever the second support is proper. Thus $\varphi$ induces the expected maps $G\to\widetilde G$. The same argument for $a^{-1}\varphi$ gives $H\to\widetilde H$; the required local finite type hypothesis for $f'$ and its etale base changes follows from local finite type base change. Naturality of the adjunction unit gives $(a^{-1}\varphi)_{T'_U}(t_U(s))=\widetilde t_U(\varphi_{T_U}(s))$. Restricting this equality to the proper-support submodules proves the naturality square for $\alpha$. This proves all clauses, including the exact support formula of Step 2.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q53-71bccff4d (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the item and its five steps in full, plus the full statement of every node they cite: the fibre-product and direct-image definitions, the module inverse-image proposition (clauses 2 and 3), the stalk-germ lemma, the zero-open lemma, local-finite-type base change, clause (1) of the closed-proper-support locality lemma and clause (2) of the closed-subset properness properties. Sources checked: Stacks more-etale.tex Tag 0F55 (lemma-base-change-f-shriek-separated). Its proof restricts the general pullback map, and the item is the adjoint form G->b_*H of that map with an explicit support formula. I also checked lines 34-42 of the refinement paragraph in blueprint main-20261015 thm-cbc-finite-torsion.proof.md, which from.place cites. This is not a target node, and no comparison isomorphism is claimed. Step 1: the identification T'_U = T_U x_X X' = T_U x_U U' holds over X', and the unit is Lambda-linear by prop (3). Step 2: the germ lemma applies with f=a, the neighbourhood (T_U, q z') and the lift condition from the commuting square; with the zero-open lemma this gives Supp t(s) = q^{-1} Supp s. Step 3: T_U->U is locally of finite type, locality (1) applies along U'->U, and U'->Y' is etale, so the section lies in H(U') = (b_*H)(U). Steps 4 and 5 are elementary naturality of the unit plus Supp phi(s) contained in Supp s, which is closed by the zero-open lemma and proper by clause (2). Small cases tested: F=0, empty X or Y', b=id, a non-flat closed-point base change and an open immersion f. No new nodes. Duplicate search found def-cbc-etale-section-proper-support, the parent composition lemma (its step 8 cites this item), the unsplit fibre-restriction citer, lem-cbc-base-change-mate-stalk and the coherent lem-pc-proper-support-* nodes; none states this map. The statement is not weakened, and separatedness is kept although unused. I accept all four declared tool_uses: stalk-germ, modules-exact, lft-base-change and closed-subset-properties (2). The report mentions a citations.json that is not in the commit; this has no effect on the DAG. No fixes.
